mention.lead_sentence: utilized lattice packing as shown in Figure 1

items.note: Twelve regular octagons in four columns of three, each column shifted half a cell against its neighbour so the slanted edges interlock and four small squares are left open at the crossings. Black hairline outline on white, no fill, no axes, no ticks, no labels, no scale - a lattice packing diagram that illustrates the space-maximising construction of the algorithm.
items.other_note: lattice packing diagram: twelve outlined octagons laid in four offset columns so their corners interlock and leave small square gaps at the joins; a printed pattern, not a plot and not a photograph

items.note: The right-hand panel of the printed figure: a three by three field of large squares drawn with rules noticeably heavier than the octagon lattice beside it, every cell empty. One of two panels under a single printed number.

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 8: Efficiency of various shapes with different values for α.
items.note: Four series plotted as markers joined by straight lines against 'Polygon Sides' (4 to 20, tick every 2) and 'Efficiency' (0.84 to 1, tick every 0.02), with light horizontal gridlines and a boxed legend inside the frame at the right keying alpha = 1.8e-7, 9.0e-8, 1.8e-8 and 1.8e-9. rules: Figures 1, 2 and 3 are line drawings rather than plots - a lattice pattern, two tessellations and one labelled polygon - so they carry family `other` with an `other_note` naming the drawing [geometry.family].

Figure 2 prints one caption over two separately measured panels standing side by side, so it takes one row per panel and both rows quote the same caption, the printed number repeated [caption.verbatim].
Figure 7 is a printed tally grid that the paper numbers as a figure, so it stays in the figure block as `table-as-figure` rather than moving to the table list [geometry.family].
Every caption in the paper prints below its exhibit and none of them states a unit or draws a conclusion, the tally grid included [caption.position].

Figures 8 to 11 are four sweeps of one efficiency curve over the same axes - Polygon Sides on x, Efficiency from 0.84 to 1 on y - differing only in the parameter varied, so all four are `line` and each carries a legend inside its frame [geometry.legend].
Only four of the eleven printed figures are named in the running text - Figures 1, 2, 4 and 7 - and the four efficiency charts are never cited by number at all [mention.count].
